g.text: FIT · PERFORMANCE ENHANCEMENT · PART 2.1 — CONTINUOUS MONITORING & WEARABLES
TIER 3 · article 3 of 15 · THE FILM TO PART 2.0'S SNAPSHOT
Bloodwork is the snapshot. This is the film.

text.tspan: Four blood draws a year tell you about four mornings. Cheap home instruments and a wrist sensor cover the other 363 days: the cuff first (the marker androgens move
first is invisible without it), the scale read two ways, a glucometer when growth signals enter, and the RHR/HRV pair that whispers "go look" days before any lab would
shout. Wire everything into one timeline, confirm trends on calibrated channels, and when a number moves: fix the cause, not the symptom.

g.text: ZONE 1 · THE STRIP CHART — SIX CONTINUOUS CHANNELS · FOUR SPARSE FLAGS
2–4 WEEKS NATURAL BASELINE FIRST — your normal is the only reference that matters.
▲ CAUGHT ON DAY 23 — next draw was 3 weeks away → cuff reading → dose adjusted
they don't tell you WHICH — they tell you to GO LOOK.
BLOODWORK TELLS YOU ABOUT THE MORNING OF THE DRAW. THIS IS THE OTHER 363 DAYS.
IF YOU BUY ONE DEVICE, BUY THIS.

text.tspan: BP is the marker androgens move first (water · sodium · red-cell mass) —
and it is completely invisible without measurement.

g.text: ARMS > ~46 cm → WRIST CUFF (arm cuffs misread on muscular arms) · SIT 5 MIN · SAME HOUR DAILY
>180/120: repeat in minutes — still high = EMERGENCY CARE, not a forum thread.

text.tspan: — strength up + scale up = TISSUE · scale up alone = FAT (surplus too high)
— a few kg overnight = WATER (usually estrogen · Pathway 3)

g.text: ↳ → BP CHANNEL ▲ — a blood-pressure warning in an aesthetics costume.
smart-scale body-fat % = trend only — DEXA/InBody owns the real number (Part 1.1).
INTERLOCK · ACTIVATES WHEN: GH · MK-677 / SECRETAGOGUES · INSULIN
with INSULIN: ESSENTIAL — dosing is a safety issue.
fasting 70–100 mg/dL · post-meal <130 · drift toward the ceiling = fix food + protocol BEFORE it's chronic.

text.tspan: regulated (long deficit) · ~37 °C normal · ≥38 °C = fever, back off

g.text: cardiovascular load · thickening blood · climbing BP · under-recovery · oncoming illness

text.tspan: a rise = reliable illness / overreach flag
the watch does NOT cuff BP —

g.text: ONE TIMELINE — every trend on it.
optical wrist sensors: excellent at YOUR TREND · mediocre at clinical
absolutes — confirm on cuff / glucometer / bloods before acting.
(the bathroom-scale rule from Part 1.1, applied to the wrist — never skip the middle step.)
ALMOST EVERY ALARM WIRES BACK TO THE HEART —
why 1.0 named it the killer · why Part 4 defends it first · mechanisms → 4.1

text.tspan: ZONE 6 · ALARM RESPONSE — FIX THE CAUSE FIRST.
"the dose is too high" is worth more than any pill that masks it.

g.text: correct cuff · corroborate wearable on a calibrated device

text.tspan: ③ THE PROTOCOL — MOST REAL ANSWERS LIVE HERE.

g.text: dose too high? compound the culprit? estrogen (→3.0)? hematocrit (→4.0)?

text.tspan: ⑤ STILL WON'T RESOLVE = THE SIGNAL

g.text: come back into range = lower the dose, or come off.
→ 1.0 BLAST REGISTER — heeding it protects your finite blasts.
THE SHOPPING LIST · IN PRIORITY ORDER
The film is rolling and the alarms are wired. Part 3.0 opens the toolbox: the eight anabolic pathways.
Harm reduction, not encouragement. Devices are screening and trend tools, not diagnostics. Over 180/120, chest pain, fainting, or a flagged rhythm = medical care now.
Home-device stack & ranges: Vigorous Steve, "Essential Health Monitoring Devices" · BP categories: American Heart Association · Wearable metrics: Whoop / Apple published feature documentation.
